channel.title: Yusuf Gadelrab — Writing
channel.description: Building in public: AI tooling, CS education research, trading systems, and free tools.

item.title: Why my portfolio has a robots.txt block list for AI crawlers that says allow
item.description: In mid-2026 everyone blocked GPTBot and ClaudeBot. I named 29 AI crawlers and allowed all of them. Here is the reasoning, and the part I can't measure.

item.title: Which AI tools I pay for, and what I run locally for free instead
item.description: I run a 30B model on my laptop for free. Here is exactly where that wins, where it loses badly, and which paid AI tools survived the comparison.

item.title: TradingView vs TrendSpider vs Stock Rover: which one a swing trader actually needs
item.description: I built my own swing screener before paying for any of the 3. Here is the honest split between charting, automated backtesting and stock screening.

item.title: The student software stack: what is free, and the four things worth paying for
item.description: Almost everything a CS student is told to buy has a free .edu tier. Here is what to claim in your first week, and the short list worth paying for.

item.title: The internship deadline panic was mostly fictional
item.description: I re-verified 18 firms against primary sources. Only two had real deadlines. One panic-inducing date belonged to a different program entirely.

item.title: Koyfin vs Seeking Alpha vs Simply Wall St: what each one is actually for
item.description: Three research tools, three different jobs: fast data, crowd opinions, visual company snapshots. Here is which 1 of the 3 is worth paying for, and why.

item.title: I wrote 30 guides in a week and here is what the schema markup taught me
item.description: TechArticle vs Article vs BlogPosting, the FAQ rule most people break, and how one Person node turned 90 pages into a single entity instead of 90 authors.

item.title: I ran a robustness test on my own trading strategy and it failed
item.description: Positive expectancy is not an edge. A risk-matched random entry captured most of mine, and what was left had a confidence interval crossing zero.

item.title: How to check a repo for secrets before you make it public
item.description: Deleting a key from a file does not delete it from git. A free, dependency-free checklist for auditing a side project before you flip it to public.

item.title: Free-first, paid-second: the build stack a broke CS student actually needs
item.description: Not licences, not AI subscriptions. The inference, hosting, data, and distribution a student needs to actually ship, for close to zero dollars.

item.title: Zero-dependency security scanner: secrets, OSV CVEs, IaC rules, git-history leaks, SBOM
item.description: Scanning for supply-chain risk usually means installing a large dependency tree first. DIRA v1.2.0 runs 7 scanners on pure stdlib Python, MIT licensed.

item.title: Two SIGCSE 2026 acceptances, and what the research found
item.description: Two SIGCSE 2026 papers as an undergraduate: what happens to a student learning to code when the programming language is English and their thinking is not.

item.title: The hardest part of an internship search isn't the applications. It's that nobody tells you when it starts
item.description: I learned this the expensive way. Summer 2027 internship recruiting is happening right now, in July 2026. Not in the spring. Not in the fall. Now.

item.title: I wrote a security scanner with zero dependencies, on purpose
item.description: Every scanner wanted a hundred packages installed before it would look for supply-chain risk. DIRA ships 7 scanners, 98 passing tests and no dependencies.

item.title: I spent months building trading strategies and then published the results that killed most of them
item.description: Months of building setups, then walk-forward testing across 4,933 trades. Exactly one survived. Here is what killed the rest, and why I published it.

item.title: I spent a day making my portfolio readable by AI instead of by humans
item.description: Recruiters ask an assistant before they open your site. If the model cannot parse you, you are not in the answer. What I changed in a single day.

item.title: I skipped the App Store and shipped 3 offline PWAs instead. Here's what that actually costs you
item.description: Apple wants $99 a year before anyone can install your thing. The honest tradeoffs of going PWA instead: what you keep, and what you genuinely give up.

item.title: I shipped a brand across 30 pages, 3 apps, 3 book covers and a clothing line in one day
item.description: Most brand systems are a folder of PNGs that quietly drift apart. One Python script generates the mark instead, so 30 pages and 3 apps never disagree.

item.title: I built three apps this week and put zero of them in the App Store
item.description: The App Store costs $99 a year and I am a broke CS student, so I shipped three PWAs instead: installable, offline, no account, and no backend at all.

item.title: I built a visa timeline planner because I got tired of being scared of a calendar
item.description: I am on TD status and it ends when I turn 21. Every explanation of the change-of-status sequence was a law firm ad or a 2019 forum post, so I built one.

item.title: How an undergrad with no connections gets into a research lab, specifically
item.description: I get asked this a lot now that I have two SIGCSE 2026 papers, so here is the actual sequence, not the inspirational version.

item.title: Built a position size calculator that refuses to let you round up. Free, no signup
item.description: Rounding 187 shares up to 200 is a silent 7% increase in risk on every trade. A free, no-signup position sizer built to refuse that.
